sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and sample text
sections.what: Imports the attachment and text reader tools and defines the shared scope sentence used by every test.
sections.why: One sentence keeps the tests comparable.
sections.watch_out: Other tests depend on this exact sentence, so changing it changes all checks.

sections.name: _docx
sections.title: Minimal Word file helper
sections.what: Writes a small Word document containing one paragraph per line of text.
sections.why: Lets the tests create a readable Word file without a Word program.
sections.watch_out: Text is inserted without escaping, so special characters could break the file.

sections.name: test_plain_email_word_and_web_documents_are_read
sections.title: Readable formats are read
sections.what: Checks that text, email, web page and Word files are all read, and that web markup is removed.
sections.why: Confirms the common readable formats work.

sections.name: test_unreadable_binary_is_kept_without_inventing_facts
sections.title: Unreadable binary is kept
sections.what: Checks that an old binary Word file yields no text, produces no evidence and is not deleted.
sections.why: Protects against inventing facts from files the app cannot read.

sections.name: test_facts_from_any_readable_document_keep_their_source
sections.title: Facts keep their source
sections.what: Checks that facts from readable email and JSON files record the source file and page.
sections.why: Lets a reviewer trace each fact back to its document.

sections.name: test_model_generation_accepts_and_reports_every_document
sections.title: Model build reports every document
sections.what: Builds a real model with one readable and one unreadable attachment and checks the manifest labels and fact links.
sections.why: Confirms the whole path from attachment to model reports each file correctly.
sections.watch_out: Depends on a sample schedule that must remain in the repository.

summary: Checks that attached documents of many kinds are read when they are readable, that unreadable files are kept without inventing facts, and that the model build reports every attachment.
purpose: Protects the rule that any readable document can supply facts with its source, and that unreadable binary files are recorded honestly.
why: Documents come in many formats, and the app must not guess content from files it cannot read.
how: A helper writes a minimal Word document. The first test writes text, email, web page and Word files and checks that each is read and has no leftover markup. The second test writes an old binary Word file and checks that nothing is extracted and the file stays on disk. The third test checks that facts from readable files keep the file name and page they came from. The fourth test builds a real model from a sample schedule, adds a readable email and an unreadable old file, and checks the manifest labels each one correctly and reports no error for the unreadable one.
inputs: Temporary folders created by the test runner, a sample schedule CSV in the samples folder, and synthetic email, web, text, JSON and Word files written by the tests.
outputs: Pass or fail results. No output files are kept after the test runs.
risks: If the Word helper produces a file the reader rejects, the readable-document test fails for a reason unrelated to the app. The sample schedule must still exist for the last test.
debug: If a readable file is missed, run the text extraction for that file type directly. If the manifest labels are wrong, compare the interpretation strings in the attachments module. If the sample is not found, check the samples folder path.
